text: The System Disposition and Integration Inventory v4 is issued in Draft status with no approval recorded.
why: This run is the D-RCV-60 realignment: no human approval step is available, the run must not stop for one, and the overlay records the missing status as an assumption.
read: Every row of v4 may be cited by the architecture, requirements and story documents of this run as the disposition and integration inventory, in Draft, and the approval is recorded afterwards by the owner of the architecture set.
impact: If the architecture owner rejects a Service cell, the affected rows and the three sheets that count them (By service, Service rules, Realignment changes) change together.

text: The In, Out, Both and Total counts of the By route sheet are calculated from the 36 interfaces: 20 In, 12 Out, 4 Both and 36 in all.
why: The sheet states that it is calculated from the Interfaces tab but every count cell is empty in v2 and v3; the route and the direction of each interface are source values, so the count adds no value that no source gives.
read: COLLINS 8 In and no Out; File 8 In and 4 Out; Direct through ACE 1 In, 3 Out and 3 Both; Through partners 1 In; Not at all today 2 In, 5 Out and 1 Both; Total 20, 12, 4 and 36.
applied_in: By route sheet, rows 5 to 10; Realignment changes R-09
impact: If an interface changes route or direction the counts change with it; the verify script recounts them from the Interfaces sheet.

text: Every Service cell is derived from the Microservice Ownership Map v1 and the scope of the 19 services in Architecture v5: the inbound ACE path goes to P1 rwb-source-data (ADR-010), the outbound file path to P2 rwb-integration unless a route service owns the content, and the route or platform service for the rest. The rule behind each group is on the Service rules sheet, SR-01 to SR-19.
why: No source names an owning service for a system or an interface, and the realignment requires the column on every row.
read: The 36 interfaces: P1 rwb-source-data 17, P6 rwb-comms 3, S5 rwb-asset 3, P2 rwb-integration 2, P9 rwb-reporting 2, and P4 rwb-access, P8 rwb-payment, P10 rwb-agent, PLT (RWB-PLT-OBS), S3 rwb-guarantee, S4 rwb-litigation, S6 rwb-debtsale, S8 rwb-deviation and S9 rwb-partner 1 each. The 25 systems: 15 rows lead with P1 rwb-source-data and 9 name one service per interface.
applied_in: Disposition and Interfaces sheets, Service column; By service sheet; Service rules sheet; Realignment changes R-02, R-03, R-04, R-08
impact: A rule that changes moves every row it covers; the By service counts and the Read me counts are recalculated from the Service column.

text: INT-19 and INT-20 and the disposition row 'Data lake and Power BI' are kept with the wording and the IDs of v3 and carry P9 rwb-reporting as the owning service; no build story is raised for them under DP-17 and ADR-018.
why: The work package keeps every ID of the source and changes only what the realignment needs; Architecture v5 removes the data lake, so the rows cannot be built, and dropping them would lose two IDs the document set may still cite.
read: A reader sees the three rows as v3 wrote them, with P9 as the service, and the Read me open point, the Key row and the Realignment changes row record that they are not built. The reporting story uses the rwb-reporting read model instead.
applied_in: Disposition row 'Data lake and Power BI'; Interfaces rows INT-19 and INT-20; Key sheet; Read me open points; Realignment changes R-06
impact: If the business later needs the reporting or model-learning output, a new interface with a free ID is raised against P9 or P7; the three rows stay as the record of what v3 said.

text: The data product of INT-06 stays 'To confirm' and no DP number is assigned.
why: The value is the source's own marker of a missing answer; assigning a DP number would invent a data product that the interface specifications and the data product catalogue do not give.
read: The row keeps the marker, and the open point of the Read me and the gap row carry the question. Every other interface row keeps its DP number or 'None' character for character.
applied_in: Interfaces sheet, row INT-06; Read me open points
impact: The data product catalogue of P1 and the interface specifications must agree before the AAL feed is built.

text: An inbound interface that ACE ingests stays owned by the ACE team and carries P1 rwb-source-data as its owning service, because only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views.
why: ADR-010 and Architecture v5 slides 7, 9 and 29 keep the views in the hands of rwb-source-data alone, and v3 gives the inbound rows the ACE team as owner and no Recovery-side service.
read: The Owner cells keep the source values; the Service cell of every inbound ACE row reads P1 rwb-source-data and the Service rules sheet gives the rule (SR-01).
applied_in: Interfaces sheet, 17 inbound rows; Disposition sheet, the inbound systems
impact: If a later change lets a service read a view directly, ADR-010 is revisited first and the affected Service cells change with it.

text: An outbound interface is owned by P2 rwb-integration when no route service owns the content, and by the route service when one does: P6 rwb-comms for INT-14, S6 rwb-debtsale for INT-25 and P9 rwb-reporting for INT-19 and INT-20.
why: Architecture v5 slide 16 gives rwb-integration the interface config, the file runs, the outbound items and the ACE integration paths, while slides 15, 17 and 19 give rwb-comms the notice, rwb-debtsale the lot and rwb-reporting the extract; the Ownership Map ruling for JOB-10 splits the WIN path the same way.
read: The Service cell names one service, the content owner, and the Service rules sheet names rwb-integration for the file build and transfer (SR-03, SR-09, SR-10).
applied_in: Interfaces rows INT-14, INT-19, INT-20, INT-25; Service rules SR-03, SR-09, SR-10
impact: If rwb-integration is given the file contract of a route service, the Service cells of the file rows move to P2.

text: INT-03 (restructure, settlement and write-off bookings) carries P8 rwb-payment as its owning service.
why: The route is 'Not at all today' and the officer books in the core bank, but the target gives rwb-payment the bookings and the posting files (Architecture v5 slide 17), which is the only service whose scope covers a booking path.
read: The row keeps Direction Out, Route 'Not at all today' and Path 'Booked by the officer; confirmed on the next day's load'; only the Service cell is new.
applied_in: Interfaces row INT-03; Service rules SR-02
impact: If booking confirmation stays entirely inside the core bank, the row needs no service and the cell is cleared in the next version.

text: INT-33 carries S4 rwb-litigation as its owning service, with S9 rwb-partner for the partner entry, and keeps Standard 'None'.
why: Architecture v5 slide 19 gives rwb-litigation enforcement and court records and slide 17 gives rwb-partner the partner instruction and result; the source names neither and gives no standard.
read: The Service cell reads S4 rwb-litigation, the Service rules sheet records the partner entry (SR-14), and the Standard and Decision cells stay 'None'.
applied_in: Interfaces row INT-33; Service rules SR-14; Read me open points
impact: The partner portal design decides whether the path moves to S9 and whether a standard is added.

text: The three statements of v3 that read as outdated are kept word for word: the Interfaces description on the reporting feeds, the Disposition description 'Supersedes v2', and the partner portal wording.
why: The rule of the run is to keep every value of the source and to change only what the realignment needs; rewording a description row is a documentation edit for the owner of the inventory.
read: The rows stay as written and the gap row records them; the Service column gives the owning service of every path meanwhile.
applied_in: Disposition row 2; Interfaces row 2; Read me open points
impact: The next full revision of the inventory rewords the two descriptions; nothing else depends on them.

text: The partner portal row and INT-24 keep the external gateway wording and carry S9 rwb-partner as the owning service.
why: Architecture v5 slide 8 puts the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) in front of rwb-partner and ADR-019 records the edge decision, while the source still says external gateway; the value is kept and the owner is derived.
read: The Path cell stays as written, the Service cell reads S9 rwb-partner, and the Service rules sheet names the partner gateway (SR-08).
applied_in: Disposition row 'Partner portal'; Interfaces row INT-24; Service rules SR-08
impact: When the partner gateway contract is written, the two cells are reworded and the standard of INT-24 is confirmed.

text: INT-21 carries P4 rwb-access, INT-22 PLT (RWB-PLT-OBS), INT-23 P10 rwb-agent, INT-24 S9 rwb-partner and INT-34 P2 rwb-integration.
why: Architecture v5 slide 30 gives the capability each service consumes: sign-in and access checks to rwb-access, audit and PII logging to every service through the platform sender, the model endpoint to rwb-agent, the partner results to rwb-partner; slide 7 and slide 16 give rwb-integration the ACE Common contract and the ACE integration paths.
read: Each row carries one service; the Service rules sheet gives the slide behind each one (SR-05 to SR-08 and SR-19); the Owner cells keep ACE team and Bank platform.
applied_in: Interfaces rows INT-21, INT-22, INT-23, INT-24, INT-34; Service rules SR-05 to SR-08, SR-19
impact: ACE Common has five consumers and no single owner in the source; the contract owner P2 is the reading of the source that keeps one Service cell per row.

text: P3 rwb-case, S1 rwb-valuation, S2 rwb-treatment and S7 rwb-writeoff own no row of the inventory, because they consume the paths through P1 and P2 rather than owning one.
why: The inventory counts systems and interfaces, not consumers, and the source gives no consuming service anywhere; adding a consumer column would change rows the realignment does not ask to change.
read: The Read me counts state 16 of the 20 owner entries and name the four services that own no row; the Service rules sheet gives the paths they use.
applied_in: Read me counts; Service rules SR-02, SR-10, SR-11
impact: A later revision may add the consumer of each path to the Service rules; the rows themselves stay as they are.

text: Every other cell of the workbook is unchanged: the 25 disposition rows and the 36 interface rows keep every source value, the Key sheet keeps its 27 rows and gains six, and the four source sheets keep their titles and description rows.
why: The rule of the run is to keep every section, ID, number and date of the source and to change only what the realignment needs, which is the Service column, the calculated counts and the document control.
read: A reader can diff v4 against v3 and find one new cell per data row and nothing else; the verify script does exactly that cell by cell.
impact: Any further change to a source cell is a new gap row.

text: The workbook properties are set to the organisation and the tool: creator Henka Group, last modified by T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash, title v4, revision 4, dated 22 November 2026.
why: The source workbook carries a person name in the author and last-modified-by properties, and root rule 4 forbids the name of a person anywhere in the output.
read: The properties name no person and no email address; the build and the verify scripts check both.
applied_in: Workbook core properties; Realignment changes R-13
impact: None on the content; a reader of the file properties sees the organisation and the tool.

text: No release date is added and no date is raised: the source carries none, and any release date written into the workbook later is tentative.
why: Dates stay unchanged and tentative (U7, DL48) and a date is never raised as a gap; the release line of the Read me says so in words.
read: The From column keeps the epic codes E1 to E8 of the source, the change-log row carries 22 November 2026, and no other date appears in the workbook.
applied_in: Read me sheet, release line and change log
impact: A release date added later is marked tentative in the same cell.
